vulnerabilities: Archipelagic geography (over 17,000 islands) makes comprehensive maritime domain awareness and defence extremely resource-intensive
Low defence spending as a share of GDP relative to regional peers, limiting force modernisation pace
South China Sea claim overlap with China near the Natuna Islands creates a recurring, unresolved friction point despite Indonesia's official non-claimant status in the broader dispute
Nickel and mineral export dependence ties Indonesia's economic fortunes to global EV/battery demand cycles it does not control
strengths: Sovereign control of the Sunda and Lombok Straits — legitimate alternative deep-water routes to the Malacca Strait, giving Indonesia unique chokepoint leverage in any Malacca-disruption scenario
Largest economy and population in ASEAN, anchoring regional diplomatic centrality (ASEAN centrality doctrine)
World's largest nickel reserves and producer, a critical input for EV batteries — a genuine 21st-century resource-leverage position
Historically effective non-aligned diplomatic tradition, maintaining working relationships with the US, China, and Russia simultaneously
